regions.text: 々群集せる中で、二人が始めて相逢うたその時にはすぐに、そのまんま、最も緊密に結びついてしまうたのである。そして耐來何ものも、我等二人にとつて、お互程に近しくはならなかつたのである』（モンテーニュ隠想婚、一、明機秀雄露、芸図七一空図入買）。

quote.translation: "By chance, on the day of a great festival in the town, among the crowds gathered there, at the time when the two of us first met, we were at once, just as we were, bound together most closely; and since then nothing has been as close to the two of us as we were to each other" (Montaigne, Essays, I, trans. Sekine Hideo, pp. 347-348).

quote.translation: What may be seen as the extreme limit of historical irrationality is the following case: "The man called Murakoshi Sanjūrō is the man who happened to be passing just in front when the famous Akechi Mitsuhide was stabbed with a bamboo spear.

quote.translation: Although he was resigned to being human refuse with nothing whatever to do with history, because he was by chance the bystander of a certain event he unexpectedly came to be noticed by history" (Tatsuno Yutaka, Riyan, p. 201).

regions.text: 支配してゐる、歴史の中には理性があるといふことを兵理として豫想してその豫想の下に「哲學的製察は偶然なものを排除するより外の意岡を有たぬ」と云ってゐる（Hegel,VorlsungenHBerdhePhilosophiederWeitgeschichte,arsgvLasson,L.S5）。

quote.translation: Hegel, on the one hand, presupposes as a truth that an ultimate purpose rules in history, that there is reason in history, and under that presupposition he says that "philosophical contemplation has no intention other than to eliminate the contingent" (Hegel, Vorlesungen über die Philosophie der Weltgeschichte, hrsg. v. Lasson, I, S. 5).

quote.translation: On the other hand, however, he also recognises the right of chance: "With regard to spirit and its activity too, we must guard against being led astray by the well-meant effort of rational cognition into pointing out as necessary phenomena that have the character of contingency, or into trying to construct them, as it is called, a priori.
